hypotheses.note: finestLC of the direction of L, transported by v ↦ v + P for EVERY origin P (stronger than one origin); second reading: subspace topology from finestLC E (facette_isOpen_induced); the two coincide (induced_finestLC_eq_finestLC)

findings: The printed proof (l.146–149) reduces openness for the finest locally convex topology to interiority in every finite-dimensional l ⊂ L. That reduction is valid for CONVEX sets (formalized as isOpen_finestLC_iff_finiteDimensional, which carries Convex), and the paper does not say at this point that a facette is convex (it is, but the proof does not show it). The Lean proof bypasses this: it applies the convex criterion to {v | v + P ∈ W}, not to F, and then uses B ± 2u ∈ W ⇒ B + u ∈ F_W(B) (add_mem_facette_of_two). Not an error in the statement; a missing step in the proof.
questions: Which topology is « sa topologie localement convexe la plus fine » of the affine variety L? Reading taken: the finest locally convex vector topology of the direction V of L (least element of the locally convex TVS topologies on V, Hausdorffness not imposed; it is Hausdorff anyway), carried to L by v ↦ v + P; proved for every P, so origin-independent. The alternative reading (L as a subspace of E with E's finest l.c. topology) is also proved (facette_isOpen_induced), and the two topologies coincide (induced_finestLC_eq_finestLC), so the reading does not affect the result.
« localement convexe » read as Mathlib's LocallyConvexSpace ℝ together with IsTopologicalAddGroup and ContinuousSMul ℝ (a locally convex topological vector space).

kb_proposals: The finest locally convex topology is Benzecri.finestLC (scaffold Chapter3/FinestLocallyConvex, Mathlib-only): the seminorm topology of ALL seminorms; finest by isLeast_finestLC; every linear map out of it into an l.c. TVS is continuous (continuous_linearMap_finestLC); a convex set is open iff algebraically open (isOpen_finestLC_iff_core / _finiteDimensional); it induces finestLC on every subspace and the module topology in finite dimension. § 5 Prop. 7 should import it.

Mathlib at the pin HAS PolynormableSpace.sInf/iInf (Analysis/LocallyConvex/WithSeminorms.lean:1059–1071) and PolynormableSpace ℝ → LocallyConvexSpace ℝ; the missing sInf lemma for LocallyConvexSpace is avoidable: define a topology by a seminorm family and get TVS/l.c. from WithSeminorms (⟨rfl⟩).

Comparing two seminorm topologies (or proving a linear map continuous into an l.c. space): WithSeminorms.continuous_of_isBounded with the target's with_gaugeSeminormFamily (𝕜 := ℝ) (E := X); the old name Seminorm.continuous_from_bounded is deprecated at the pin.

A convex C is a neighbourhood of a core point x for finestLC: U = (x+·)⁻¹'C ∩ −(x+·)⁻¹'C is convex, balanced (balanced_iff_neg_mem), absorbent (absorbent_iff_eventually_nhdsNE_zero), and gauge_lt_one_subset_self puts the gaugeSeminorm unit ball inside U.

With a topology given by letI on a type V, a Submodule of V picks up the subtype instance, not finestLC: pass topologies explicitly (@Continuous.isOpen_preimage _ _ t₁ t₂ f hf _ h) when both appear. Submodule.linearProjOfIsCompl is deprecated at the pin: use Submodule.projectionOnto / projectionOnto_apply_left.
